resources.string: Checks sender, links, attachments and wording against rules; the result shows as a banner in the mail and as a symbol in the list. Everything runs on this phone, nothing is sent anywhere.
Only new mails and mails you open are checked. Older mail is not scanned.

After fetching, mails that are spam by fixed rules go to the account’s spam folder (without a spam folder only a grey symbol). Never from contacts, people you wrote to, trusted or allowed senders. Please check the spam folder now and then.
Uses the phishing check: switch the protection on first.
Take over the server’s spam mark
Your mail server’s DMARC or SPF check says the sender is forged.
Off by default: better to see a warning than to miss a mail.
Mails from these addresses or domains are spam.
Mails from these addresses or domains are never spam.
Please enter an address (name@example.com) or a domain (example.com).
Reads QR codes and the text of images in the mail, for example a fake bank logo used as a link. Only on this device.
Ask the local AI in the grey zone
Helper connected. For mails with some signs, the model tells who the mail claims to be and what it asks for; the rules decide. It can only raise a warning, never lower one.
Needs the NovaBird Helper (Settings › Semantic search and AI). No cloud.
Allowed: addresses from your contacts get no “new sender” hint, and a known name with a new address is reported.
Not allowed: contacts do not count. The check still works, with more “new sender” hints.

No more warnings for these addresses. Forgery hints stay: failed sender checks (DMARC, SPF, DKIM), look-alike links, disguised attachments, extortion. A sender of a mail rated “dangerous” cannot be added with a tap, only here.
Your contacts and people you have written to are not in this list; they count as known anyway.
Please enter a complete email address.
This filter is meant to protect you from malicious mails. It checks every new and every opened mail against rules, on this phone only.
The filter is by no means perfect. It can miss a dangerous mail, and it can warn about a harmless one. A missing warning is not a guarantee that a mail is safe.
Whatever you do with a mail — open a link, reply, download or open an attachment, pay — remains your own decision and your own responsibility.
I have read and understood this.
